page: Microsoft Azure D48ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DADSv5 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor. This x86_64 architecture server features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as a local 1843 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators are present.

In benchmark evaluations, the D48ads_v5 demonstrates strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, scoring in the top 25% on stress-ng and PassMark CPU tests. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench ray tracing, and image processing also register in the top tier. Memory performance is robust, with a strong PassMark memory score, though raw memory bandwidth for large blocks remains in the average range. Cryptographic tasks perform exceptionally well, as evidenced by a strong PassMark encryption score, aided by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instructions.

While the server excels in compute-heavy multi-threaded tasks, it exhibits clear performance limitations in large-scale machine learning workloads. LLM text generation using a large 70B model falls into the bottom 10% at 2.54 tokens/sec, indicating a poor fit for heavy AI inference without dedicated GPU acceleration. However, it maintains average performance for smaller model prompt processing and text generation. Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, high-capacity local SSD, and strong multi-core capabilities, this instance is well-suited for relational databases, multi-threaded software compilation, web serving, and general-purpose enterprise workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D48ads_v5 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine powered by a dedicated 48-vCPU AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz. It features 192.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 1843 GB local SSD. Benchmark data highlights strong multi-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng and PassMark CPU tests, alongside strong cryptographic and image processing capabilities. However, memory bandwidth and database operations perform in the average tier, and text generation for large 70B LLM models is poor, reflecting the lack of GPU acceleration. This resource profile makes the D48ads_v5 highly effective for multi-threaded enterprise applications, software compilation, and database hosting, offering a balanced ratio of compute, memory, and high-speed local storage.
